subject.title: Centralize chat-session naming; define subagent session lifetime & cross-channel persistence

question: What canonical naming, lifetime, and persistence contract should OpenClaw expose for ACP/native subagent sessions across Gateway, channel bindings, and companion apps?
rationale: Current code has useful partial mechanisms, but selecting how parent-owned runs, session-mode subagents, persistent bindings, one-shot ACP sessions, and companion app visibility interact is product/API policy rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Define the core contract first
options.body: Establish one title resolver and explicit lifecycle classes for parent-owned run sessions, kept session-mode sessions, persistent bindings, and one-shot ACP sessions, then update docs/tests around that model.

options.title: Centralize naming first
options.body: Make titles consistent now while leaving lifetime and cross-channel persistence as narrower follow-up items, reducing UX friction but preserving policy ambiguity.

options.title: Defer core changes
options.body: Keep the current per-surface behavior and handle only companion UI filtering, accepting ongoing inconsistency in core session semantics.

recommendation.title: Define the core contract first
recommendation.body: Establish one title resolver and explicit lifecycle classes for parent-owned run sessions, kept session-mode sessions, persistent bindings, and one-shot ACP sessions, then update docs/tests around that model.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation trace across the affected gateway, agents, and ACP files points most strongly to this owner for deciding the cross-surface direction.
